purpose: Test whether normalising each sample's own prototype-distance vector (no Test-batch statistic at all) removes the session-induced shift and improves the Test S1-vs-S2 diagnostic AUC, rather than merely moving the operating point.

score_definitions.raw: score = -d1 (negative nearest same-task prototype distance; E143 baseline, higher = more registered)
score_definitions.z_profile: score = max_j ((-d_j - median(-d)) / IQR(-d)) = (median(d) - d1) / IQR(d); per-sample median/IQR of the sample's own same-task prototype distances
score_definitions.softmax_profile: score = max_j softmax(-d_j / tau) = exp(-d1/tau) / sum_j exp(-d_j/tau); tau = per-task median of Train OOF nearest distances
score_definitions.rank_profile: score = 1 - (#{j : d_j <= d1} / #prototypes); structural diagnostic (the nearest distance is always the minimum, so this is constant within a task)
score_definitions.ratio_d2_d1: score = d2 / d1; d2 = nearest prototype belonging to a different identity than the nearest prototype. Larger = the runner-up identity is farther relative to the best match, i.e. a cleaner margin and more likely registered
score_definitions.gap: score = d2 - d1; higher = cleaner identity separation
score_definitions.rank_ref_control: score = 1 - ECDF_{Train-OOF, same task}(d1); monotone transform of raw, included only as a control showing that rank calibration cannot change AUC

protocol: E143 clean protocol: per-task standardisation and PCA-96 fitted on Train fit_rows (frac<=0.6); LOSO excludes the scored identity and builds prototypes only from fit_rows; five sequential Train OOF blocks calibrate thresholds; Test is score-only; session labels are diagnostic only.
